message.content:
During the 19th century the most celebrated sculpture was **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (completed 1889).  
It became an icon of Romanticism and modern art, widely reproduced and admired worldwide.  

Other notable 19th‑century masterpieces include:

| Artist | Sculpture | Year |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Antonio Canova | *Psyche Revived by Cupid’s Kiss* | 1787–1793 (late 18th, still influential in the 19th) |
| Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux | *La Danse* (for the Paris Exposition) | 1875 |
| Auguste Rodin | *The Gates of Hell* (project began 1880) | 1880–1917 |
| Hiram Powers | *The Greek Slave* | 1844 |

But if you’re looking for the single work that defined 19th‑century sculpture for the public imagination, “The Kiss” is usually cited.
